title: Password UX Best Practices
summary: This lesson covers essential UX improvements for password fields, emphasizing that password length is more important than complexity rules. It demonstrates real-time validation, strength meters, and the importance of supporting password managers for a seamless signup experience.

transcript.text: Capital P, at sign, zero. Passes every rule. Cracks in 2 hours.
Strength is entropy, not checkboxes. Length beats symbols.
Show the checklist while they type. Each requirement ticks live. Green before they hit the button.
A red bar says weak, a growing bar says almost. Strength meters coach in real time. Errors only punish after the fact.
Masked dots cause typos. Give them the eye toggle. And never block paste.
Password managers type stronger passwords than humans.
The strongest pattern: offer the password. Built into iOS, Android and every modern browser. One tap. Generated, unique, saved. Zero typing, zero weak choices, zero reuse.
Follow for more form UX and save this for your next signup flow.

on_screen_text: Green before they hit the button.
before_after: Moving from static error messages shown after submission to real-time coaching via live checklists and strength meters that update as the user types.
